resource.description: The resource, one of: thread/<key>: one thread: its label and link, its tickets and latest decisions, and its triggers, newest first; ticket/<id>: a ticket's card, the trigger, decision and threads it is tied to, its latest assignments with the start of each report, and its inputs, newest first; ticket/<id>/assignment: its assignment text; ticket/<id>/assignments: its assignments, newest first, with the start of each report; ticket/<id>/inputs: its inputs, newest first; ticket/<id>/result: its latest report; ticket/<id>/report/<id>: the report of one of its assignments; ticket/<id>/transcript: its Executor Session's messages, newest first; ticket/<id>/message/<n>: one message of that transcript; ticket/<id>/input/<id>: one input it was delivered; trigger/<id>: a trigger's text, where it went, the message it replies to and the messages around it on its thread; prompts/<revision>: one prompt version by number, or current, the one the Session works under; feishu/<trigger-id>/…: a Feishu original, as the dsh-superagent-feishu skill describes; github/…: a GitHub original, as the dsh-superagent-github skill describes.

offset.description: Copy next_offset from the previous page; it counts characters of a text and items of a list.

limit.description: Characters of a text, 4000 by default and 8000 at most, or items of a list, 20 by default and 50 at most.

trigger_id.description: The candidate card's trigger_id; deciding it decides its batch.

title.description: accept: a short label of at most 200 characters describing the original request; no added requirements or implementation advice.

worktree_name.description: accept: Meaningful short English ticket name, e.g. fix-plan-color. Translate Chinese titles into English; no Chinese, pinyin or generic ticket names. 1–4 lowercase words in kebab-case, at most 32 characters.

acknowledgement.description: accept: one brief sentence of at most 100 words naming the concrete change and intended result in the source language. It is posted as a reply to the original source on acceptance, so do not quote the source; quote an earlier proposal briefly only when the trigger merely confirms it and the sentence does not already state it. No generic I will handle it.

note.description: accept and attach: Optional routing background or explicit human constraint, at most 30 words. Never add implementation instructions or replace the original source.

reason.description: ignore and stop: why, at most 500 characters; an ignore needs it.

trigger_id.description: Original candidate ID returned by orchestrator_eval; every reference is scoped to this trigger.

message_id.description: Only for message: omit for the trigger, or the id of a window message or stub.

cursor.description: Only for thread: omit on the first page, then the next_cursor of the window or the cursor of next_read. Never a thread or message ID.

image_id.description: Only for image: an image id the window or a read lists.

offset.description: Text pagination: copy next_offset; keep the other arguments unchanged. Images use 0.

worktree_name.description: Meaningful short English ticket name, e.g. fix-plan-color. Translate Chinese titles into English; no Chinese, pinyin or generic ticket names. 1–4 lowercase words in kebab-case, at most 32 characters.

intent_evidence.description: For acceptance: the quotes that establish the three facts.

acknowledgement.description: For acceptance: one sentence in the source language, posted as a reply to the trigger; omit only when a matched rule asks for silence.

trigger_id.description: The original human question, for an answer only.

human_action.description: Required for attention: the ticket's current attention question.

thread.description: Thread key, for example github:123 or feishu:<chat>:<root message>

block.description: pause pauses or resumes processing: new Evals, dispatch and replies.

source.description: With block source: the Source instance id, such as github or feishu.

value.description: The whole block; a Source takes { enabled, config }, pause takes { paused }.

revision.description: The block's revision; pause ignores it.

overrides.description: Text in place of a built-in part, by its key in prompts/defaults; a part not named follows its built-in text.

base.description: Key of the built-in text it was edited from; copy as read, or omit.

baseRevision.description: The revision the configuration edits; required unless preview is set.

preview.description: true saves nothing: it composes both roles' prompts from the configuration and returns their prompt-preview resources.

text.description: At most 100 words; Markdown is supported.

thread.description: The thread key, which trigger/<id> of one of its messages shows as thread, such as feishu:<chat>:<root> or github:<number>.

reason.description: One sentence on why the thread is not about this ticket.
How it relates, in one sentence.
One sentence on what it asks for beyond this ticket.

human_action.description: One concrete question for a person, also with state=progress; omit to keep the pending one, null to clear it.

question_for_trigger_id.description: With human_action: the human message that raised the question, which is asked where that person wrote.

pr_number.description: The ticket's PR: its source PR, or one by bot from a branch named after this ticket (DSH_SUPERAGENT_NAME).

reply_to_trigger_id.description: The explicit human question this report answers; never for ordinary progress.

script.description: The workflow script: an absolute path, or one relative to cwd.

cwd.description: The absolute directory every node of the run works in.

args.description: The value the script reads as args.

pair.description: The compute pair every node runs on; without it, the Source's pair, else the Executor's default.

trigger_id.description: The trigger of the request this run answers; starting with the same trigger, script, cwd and args again returns the run it started.
